items.followUp: Define friction and write two ways to increase it.

rubric.why: The definition identifies friction as opposing relative motion between surfaces in contact.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that friction opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact.

rubric.why: Lubrication reduces friction between surfaces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning oil, grease, or another lubricant.

rubric.why: Smoothing the surfaces reduces friction.
rubric.description: Names smoothing surfaces as a method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that polishing or smoothing the surfaces reduces friction.

rubric.why: Ball bearings replace sliding friction with smaller rolling friction.
rubric.description: Names ball bearings as a method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the use of ball bearings or rollers.

modelAnswer: Friction is the force that opposes the relative motion, or tendency of relative motion, between two surfaces in contact.
Friction can be reduced by applying a lubricant such as oil or grease.
Friction can be reduced by polishing or smoothing the surfaces.
Friction can be reduced by using ball bearings or rollers.

items.followUp: A force of 50 N makes an angle of 30° with the positive x-axis. Find its perpendicular x- and y-components.

rubric.why: The component equations require a stated angle convention.
rubric.description: Identifies the angle used for resolving the vector.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that θ is measured from the positive x-axis.

rubric.why: The horizontal component is the projection of F along the x-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fx = F cos θ.

rubric.why: The vertical component is the projection of F along the y-axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fy = F sin θ.

rubric.why: The question asks for perpendicular components, which lie along mutually perpendicular axes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the x- and y-components as perpendicular components.

modelAnswer: Let θ be the angle between vector F and the positive x-axis.
The perpendicular x-component is Fx = F cos θ.
The perpendicular y-component is Fy = F sin θ.
These components act along the mutually perpendicular x- and y-axes.

items.followUp: A ball of mass 200 g moves at 10 m s⁻¹. Calculate its kinetic energy.

rubric.why: The mass must be converted from grams to kilograms before substitution in SI units.
rubric.description: Converts the given mass to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining m = 0.5 kg.

rubric.why: This is the formula for kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for KE = ½mv².

rubric.why: Correct substitution and evaluation give the numerical kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution of 0.5 kg and 20 m s⁻¹; award 1 mark for evaluating to 100.

rubric.why: The kinetic energy is 100 joules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 100 J.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 500 g = 0.5 kg, v = 20 m s⁻¹.
Formula: KE = ½mv².
Substitution: KE = ½ × 0.5 kg × (20 m s⁻¹)².
KE = 100 kg m² s⁻² = 100 J.

items.followUp: Write four properties of a suitable thermometric liquid.

rubric.why: Uniform expansion gives a reliable temperature scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that the liquid expands uniformly with temperature.

rubric.why: The liquid should not cling to the glass tube.
rubric.description: States that it does not wet or stick to glass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

rubric.why: A low freezing point allows measurement at low temperatures.
rubric.description: States that it has a low freezing point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

rubric.why: A high boiling point allows measurement at higher temperatures.
rubric.description: States that it has a high boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

modelAnswer: A thermometric liquid should expand uniformly with temperature.
It should not wet or stick to the glass of the thermometer.
It should have a low freezing point.
It should have a high boiling point.

items.followUp: Differentiate between circular motion and vibratory motion.

rubric.why: Linear motion follows a straight-line path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an object moves along a straight line.

rubric.why: Random motion has no fixed path or direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the motion is irregular or has no definite direction/path.

modelAnswer: Linear motion: motion of an object along a straight-line path.
Random motion: motion of an object along an irregular path with no definite direction.

items.followUp: Define the centre of gravity of a body.

rubric.why: The centre of mass is described as a single representative point for the body's mass.
rubric.description: Identifies it as a point representing the body's mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a point at which the body's mass may be considered concentrated.

rubric.why: The definition refers to the distribution of mass throughout the body.
rubric.description: Relates the point to the body's mass distribution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the point to the body's mass distribution.

modelAnswer: The centre of mass is the point at which the whole mass of a body may be considered to be concentrated.
Its position represents the distribution of mass of the body.

items.followUp: What is the moment of a couple, and what does it depend on?

rubric.why: A couple consists of two forces of equal magnitude.
rubric.description: States that the forces are equal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the two forces have equal magnitude.

rubric.why: The forces act in opposite directions and along different parallel lines of action.
rubric.description: States that the forces are opposite and parallel with separated lines of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they act in opposite directions along different parallel lines of action.

modelAnswer: A couple is formed when two equal and opposite parallel forces act on the same body along different lines of action.
The forces are separated by a perpendicular distance, so they produce a turning effect.
